title: Regular base change for closed supported etale inverse image
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $r:P\to X$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible; Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $r$ is regular, meaning flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] with geometrically regular fibres: the fibre over a point remains regular after every finite extension of its residue field [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and form $Z_P=P\times_XZ$ with projections $q:Z_P\to Z$ and $i_P:Z_P\hookrightarrow P$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the small-etale bounded-below derived categories of $\Lambda$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], ordinary inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], which are exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact], and the supported right derived inverse image $i^!$ of the functor $i^{-1}\ker(1\to j_*j^{-1})$, where $j$ is the complementary open immersion [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. For every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ the canonical supported comparison is an isomorphism
$$q^*i^!M\xrightarrow{\sim}i_P^!r^*M.$$
The comparison is the adjunction mate of closed direct-image base change: after applying $i_{P*}$, its composite with the supported counit equals $r^*$ of the supported counit $i_*i^!M\to M$. These comparisons are natural in $M$, commute with Tate twists and shifts, and satisfy pasting for compositions of regular base changes and for compositions of closed immersions. They commute with restriction to open subschemes and localization at points, including the supported-composition identifications defining successive point costalks. No excellence, finite-type, compactifiability, or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Corollary 4.2.3 and its proof from Proposition 4.2.1; canonical supported comparison and its fibrewise use in Lemma 4.3.1.1. The pasting/localization clauses specify the canonical mate, not arbitrary comparison isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] with $n=1$, $h=r$, $a=i$, $Y=P$, $Z\prime=Z_P$, $a\prime=i_P$, and $h\prime=q$. Identify $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$ with $\mathbf F_\ell$; this is the same constant coefficient ring, so the module categories, exact inverse images and supported kernel functors are the same. Its hypotheses are exactly regularity of $r$, Noetherianness of $P,X$, invertibility of $\ell$, and the closed immersion $i$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $B_{r,i,M}:q^*i^!M\longrightarrow i_P^!r^*M$ for every bounded-below $M$, without excellence or constructibility. The same cited statement supplies naturality, shifts, roots-of-unity twists, restriction to opens, and localization at points; these clauses also specialize at $n=1$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Corollary 4.2.3 and Lemma 4.3.1.1; canonical counit normalization made explicit using the adjunction mate formula

proof.text: Fix the normalization of this canonical comparison. Write $\varepsilon_i:i_*i^!\to1$ and $\varepsilon_{i_P}:i_{P*}i_P^!\to1$ for the supported counits. The localization-triangle comparison in [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] commutes with these counits. In the notation of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], take $L_1=i_*$, $R_1=i^!$, $L_2=i_{P*}$, $R_2=i_P^!$, $G=q^*$, $H=r^*$ and let $\alpha:i_{P*}q^*\xrightarrow{\sim}r^*i_*$ be closed direct-image base change in this orientation. The counit compatibility reads $\varepsilon_{i_P,r^*M}\circ i_{P*}B_{r,i,M}=r^*(\varepsilon_{i,M})\circ\alpha_{i^!M}$. The transpose characterization in the cited definition says precisely that $B_{r,i}$ is the mate of $\alpha$. In particular the normalization specifies the actual arrow, not just its isomorphism class.

source.place: Expose XVII, Corollary 4.2.3 and Lemma 4.3.1.1; canonical counit normalization made explicit using the adjunction mate formula

proof.text: For successive regular base changes $P\xleftarrow{s}Q$, put $Z_Q=Q\times_XZ$ and let $t:Z_Q\to Z_P$ be the projection. The composition clause of [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change], at $n=1$, gives $B_{rs,i,M}=B_{s,i_P,r^*M}\circ t^*(B_{r,i,M})$ under pullback-composition identifications. For successive closed immersions $W\xrightarrow{k}Z\xrightarrow{i}X$, identify $(ik)^!$ with $k^!i^!$ by [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition], with its pasted counit. The successive-supported-restriction clause of [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] is therefore the canonical right-adjoint comparison. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], applied to these two closed adjunctions and their pullbacks, identifies the exchange for $ik$ with the two successive exchanges: after writing $k_P:W_P\to Z_P$ and $u:W_P\to W$, it is $k_P^!(B_{r,i,M})\circ B_{q,k,i^!M}:u^*k^!i^!M\to k_P^!i_P^!r^*M$. Thus both asserted pasting laws hold with the counit normalization from step 2.

source.place: Expose XVII, Corollary 4.2.3 and Lemma 4.3.1.1; canonical counit normalization made explicit using the adjunction mate formula

proof.text: The localization and successive-closed-restriction clauses of [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] also give the point-costalk assertion, without any assumption on excellence. Explicitly, to restrict at $z\in Z$, first restrict the ambient scheme to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,z}$, restrict $Z$ to its inverse image there, and then take the closed-point supported restriction. The cited statement identifies taking this costalk of $i^!M$ on $Z$ with taking the costalk of $M$ on $X$. Its compatibility with localization and successive supported restrictions says that doing these operations on the comparison in step 1 gives the same arrow as forming the comparison after localization and then composing supported restrictions. Together with step 3 this supplies the requested successive point-costalk identifications, and completes all clauses.
